sourcedFrom: IWI MASADA™ Semi Automatic Pistol 9X19mm Parabellum Operation Manual — 08.011.18.01.00A (2019)
cleanIntro: IWI's published strip for the striker-fired Masada: slide locked back, disassembly lever down ninety degrees, trigger pressed to release the slide, then recoil spring and barrel out. Six steps and IWI stops there — the book's own note is that further disassembly is not recommended and voids the warranty.

steps.title: Magazine out, slide back, chambered round ejected
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction throughout. Press the magazine catch and take the magazine out first — always the magazine before the chamber, or you feed a fresh round into the chamber you just cleared. Then pull the slide fully to the rear and let any chambered cartridge eject.
steps.aside: Pull the slide to the rear and eject any chambered cartridge.
steps.quote: Press the magazine catch and remove the magazine.
steps.cite: IWI MASADA™ Semi Automatic Pistol 9X19mm Parabellum Operation Manual — 08.011.18.01.00A — Unloading the Pistol, step 1, printed p.12 (PDF page 34)

steps.title: Chamber, breech face and magazine well checked by eye and by finger
steps.action: Hold the slide back and check the chamber and breech face are free of ammunition — then check the magazine well too, and IWI asks you to inspect physically as well as visually. Their reason is worth taking seriously: poor light or carbon buildup in the gun genuinely can hide a case. A finger in the chamber settles what a glance leaves in doubt. Then release the slide.
steps.aside: Visually inspect the chamber, breech face and magazine well, as well as physically inspecting these areas to ensure there is no ammunition.
steps.quote: While the slide is in the rear position, visually check to make certain that the chamber and breech face are free of ammunition.
steps.cite: IWI MASADA™ Semi Automatic Pistol 9X19mm Parabellum Operation Manual — 08.011.18.01.00A — Unloading the Pistol, step 3, printed p.12 (PDF page 34)
steps.warn: It may be difficult to see into the chamber area because of poor lighting or carbon buildup in the gun.

steps.title: Every magazine checked, work surface cleared
steps.action: Before the pistol comes apart, IWI's caution covers more than the gun in your hand: ALL magazines unloaded, and nothing left in the chamber. The strip ends with a deliberate trigger press on a slide that is forward, so a round anywhere in the system is the one thing that turns that step into a discharge. Lay the pistol out on a clean surface and keep the parts in the order they come off.
steps.aside: Disassembly should be carried out on a clean surface. All the disassembled parts should be placed in order of their removal.
steps.quote: Before disassembling the pistol, ensure all magazines are unloaded and no ammunition is left in the chamber.
steps.cite: IWI MASADA™ Semi Automatic Pistol 9X19mm Parabellum Operation Manual — 08.011.18.01.00A — DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY, General, CAUTION, printed p.15 (PDF page 37)

steps.title: Slide pulled back and locked on the slide catch lever
steps.action: Pull the slide rearward and at the same moment press UP on the slide catch lever so the slide locks open. The Masada has ambidextrous slide catch levers, so use whichever hand suits — the motion is simultaneous, not sequential, and the slide has to be far enough back for the catch to find its notch.
steps.quote: While pulling the slide rearward (1) (Fig. 14), simultaneously press upward on the slide catch lever to lock the slide (2) (Fig. 15).
steps.cite: IWI MASADA™ Semi Automatic Pistol 9X19mm Parabellum Operation Manual — 08.011.18.01.00A — Disassembling the Pistol, step 1, printed p.16 (PDF page 38)

steps.title: Disassembly lever rotated down 90 degrees
steps.action: With the slide held open, rotate the disassembly lever DOWN through ninety degrees. It is a separate control from the slide catch — do not confuse the two. Until this lever is down the slide will not leave the frame no matter what else you do, and forcing the slide with the lever up is how the frame rails get marked.
steps.quote: Rotate the disassembly lever down 90 degrees (Fig. 16).
steps.cite: IWI MASADA™ Semi Automatic Pistol 9X19mm Parabellum Operation Manual — 08.011.18.01.00A — Disassembling the Pistol, step 2, printed p.16 (PDF page 38)

steps.title: Slide released forward under control, trigger pressed, slide off
steps.action: Release the slide and walk it forward slowly — it is under recoil spring tension the whole way and IWI says so explicitly. With the slide forward, press the trigger and the slide comes off the front of the frame. That trigger press is a real trigger press on a striker gun, which is precisely why every magazine had to be checked and the chamber confirmed empty two steps ago.
steps.aside: Pull the trigger when the slide is forward to remove the slide from the frame (Fig. 17).
steps.quote: Release the slide and slowly pull the slide forward on the frame - carefully, as it is under tension from the recoil spring.
steps.cite: IWI MASADA™ Semi Automatic Pistol 9X19mm Parabellum Operation Manual — 08.011.18.01.00A — Disassembling the Pistol, step 3, printed p.17 (PDF page 39)
steps.warn: This step requires pressing the trigger. Confirm the chamber is empty and every magazine is out of the pistol and out of reach before your finger goes near it.

steps.title: Recoil spring eased forward and lifted out of the slide
steps.action: The recoil spring sits in its housing under the barrel. Push it slowly TOWARDS THE FRONT of the barrel to unseat it, then lift the spring and its guide up and out of the slide. Slowly is the operative word — the assembly is captive but still sprung, and letting it go is how the guide ends up across the room.
steps.aside: Lift the recoil spring and recoil spring guide up and out of the slide (Fig. 18).
steps.quote: Remove the recoil spring from its housing under the barrel by slowly pushing the spring towards the front of the barrel.
steps.cite: IWI MASADA™ Semi Automatic Pistol 9X19mm Parabellum Operation Manual — 08.011.18.01.00A — Disassembling the Pistol, step 5, printed p.17 (PDF page 39)

steps.title: Barrel lifted out of the slide by its lug
steps.action: Lift the barrel out of the slide by pulling UP on the barrel lug. The Masada is a short-recoil, lug-to-slot design — the barrel's lugs sit in slots in the slide — so with the recoil spring gone the barrel simply rises out at the rear and comes free. It does not go forward out of the muzzle.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel from the slide by pulling up on the barrel lug (Fig. 19).
steps.cite: IWI MASADA™ Semi Automatic Pistol 9X19mm Parabellum Operation Manual — 08.011.18.01.00A — Disassembling the Pistol, step 6, printed p.17 (PDF page 39)

steps.title: Field strip complete — four pieces, and IWI stops here
steps.action: Slide, frame, barrel and recoil spring assembly. That is the whole strip in the book, and IWI names those four plus the back strap and its pin as the pistol's parts. The back strap changes with a 2.5 mm punch if you want a different grip size, and the magazine comes apart for cleaning. Nothing else does: further disassembly is stated to be not recommended and to void all warranties.
steps.quote: Disassembling or assembling of any other parts is not recommended and will void all warranties.
steps.cite: IWI MASADA™ Semi Automatic Pistol 9X19mm Parabellum Operation Manual — 08.011.18.01.00A — DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY, General, printed p.15 (PDF page 37)
steps.warn: We do not recommend further disassembly of this pistol.

deepAbsentReason: There is no deeper cleaning procedure to author. The Masada book publishes exactly three disassembly procedures — the six-step pistol strip (printed pp.16-17), changing the back strap (printed p.18), and magazine disassembly (printed pp.21-23) — and its CARE AND CLEANING chapter (printed pp.28-30) calls for nothing beyond the strip plus the magazines. IWI bounds it twice in the document's own words: "Disassembling or assembling of any other parts is not recommended and will void all warranties" on printed p.15, and "We do not recommend further disassembly of this pistol. Any other maintenance or repairs must be performed by a factory warranty repair station" on printed p.23. The pistol is striker-fired and the book gives no striker, extractor or sear procedure at all. Nothing was constructed from the parts overview drawings.

cleaning.name: BARREL, CHAMBER & BORE
tasks: Run the brass wire brush completely through the chamber and bore until it protrudes from the far end, then pull it back out and repeat several times
Clean the bore with a patch moistened with gun cleaning solvent, then repeat with clean dry patches
Leave the chamber and bore DRY — no oil deposits

cleaning.name: SLIDE
tasks: Work around the extractor and the firing pin channel until all carbon buildup and powder residue is gone
Use a small brush, swabs and solvent for the areas that cannot be reached otherwise
Remove any heavy or sticky protective grease, especially on a new pistol
Leave the breech face of the slide dry

cleaning.name: FRAME & MOVING PARTS
tasks: Oil all moving parts with a lightly oiled patch or cloth, then take the excess off with a dry one
Inspect every part for wear, cracks or damage as you go
Check the surfaces are free from rust and that any chrome coating is not peeling

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Care and cleaning includes the magazines — do not skip them
Hold the magazine spring with a thumb while the base comes off; it is under pressure and can let go
Do not point the magazine base at anyone's face, and wear eye protection
Push down on the follower and slide it out through the base opening to clean the body

reassembly: Insert the muzzle end of the barrel into the slide, then seat the barrel into its rearmost, locked position.
Press the recoil spring down towards the barrel and make sure it is securely fitted into the recess in the bottom lug of the barrel.
Mount the slide on the frame, run it rearward so the frame rails align with the slide rails, take it all the way back and lock it with the slide catch lever.
Move the disassembly lever UP through 90 degrees to lock the slide on the frame.
Release the slide by pressing the slide catch lever, or by pulling the slide fully to the rear and letting it go.
On a pistol fitted with the optional manual safety, move the safety lever to SAFE.
fncheck: IWI's own closing check after cleaning is to assemble the pistol and make sure it functions properly — cycle the slide and confirm it returns fully into battery, confirm the disassembly lever is back up at 90 degrees and the slide is locked to the frame, confirm the slide catch levers work from both sides, and seat an empty magazine to confirm the catch holds it. On models fitted with the optional manual safety, move the safety lever to the SAFE position; check whether yours has one, because it is fitted only to some models.
